communication.title: Communication
communication.channels.subtitle: Connect messaging channels and bind them to your primary agent
communication.channels.setupHint: Expand a channel, paste credentials, pick the agent that should answer, then Save & connect. Pairing-enabled channels (Telegram) still need an approved pairing request before DMs work.
communication.channels.multiInstanceHint: You can run several accounts of the same type (e.g. two Signal numbers), each with its own agent. Use Add instance above, or “Add … instance” on a card.
communication.channels.orPerCard: or on a card: Add signal / telegram / … instance
communication.channels.addAnotherTip: Another {{type}} account/bot with its own credentials and agent
communication.channels.deleteConfirm: Delete channel instance “{{name}}”? Credentials for this instance will be removed.
communication.channels.mode.autonomousTi: Autonomous — runs unattended (graduated-autonomy ladder gates each action). Click to set Managed.
communication.channels.mode.managedTip: Managed — the security gate governs every tool call. Click to set Autonomous.
communication.channels.secretPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep current value
communication.setup.signal.intro: EYAS does not embed Signal. You run signal-cli (or a small REST container) once; then paste only two values here.
communication.setup.signal.step1: Install signal-cli (e.g. brew install signal-cli) OR run the bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api Docker image with MODE=json-rpc.
communication.setup.signal.step2: Register or link a bot number (prefer a separate number, not your personal Signal): signal-cli link -n "EYAS" and scan the QR, or register + SMS verify.
communication.setup.signal.step3: Start the HTTP API so it listens locally, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080 (native daemon or container port publish).
communication.setup.signal.step4: Below: enter the bot phone number in international form (+36…) and the bridge base URL (no path).
communication.setup.signal.step5: Choose the EYAS agent that should answer, then Save & connect. Message the bot number from your phone.
communication.setup.telegram.intro: You need a free bot from Telegram’s @BotFather (about 1 minute).
communication.setup.telegram.step2: Send /newbot, pick a display name and a username ending in “bot”.
communication.setup.telegram.step3: Copy the HTTP API token BotFather gives you (looks like 123456:ABC-DEF…).
communication.setup.telegram.step4: Paste the token below, choose which EYAS agent should answer, then Save & connect.
communication.setup.telegram.step5: Message your bot on Telegram. Approve the pairing code under Communication → Pairing.
communication.field.signal-account-numbe: The Signal number linked to signal-cli — not your personal chat partner’s number
communication.field.signal-cli-url.label: Bridge base URL
communication.field.signal-cli-url.hint: Where signal-cli REST / HTTP is listening (no /api/… path)
communication.field.telegram-bot-token.h: Telegram → @BotFather → /newbot → “Use this token to access the HTTP API”
communication.channels.agentHint: Inbound messages on this channel run this agent. Defaults to your primary assistant when you first save.
communication.channels.connectionsManage: Channel connections are managed via configuration
communication.channels.empty: No communication channels in the catalog.
communication.inbound.subtitle: Durable at-least-once queue of inbound channel messages. Failed deliveries back off and dead-letter; dead rows can be re-queued.
communication.pairing.subtitle: Unknown channel senders get a pairing code and wait here for approval. Approving grants the channel access to its bound agent; pairings survive restarts.
